{"id":"ef80fee5-55e9-4309-afbc-d4506e5aab5c","object":"chat.completion","created":1790552640,"model":"deepseek-flash","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"","reasoning_content":"The review_patch simulation returned zero violations and properties: deterministic true, retry_safe true, idempotent true, state_isolated true, injection_safe true; pure false, read_only false, fault_covered false.

My declared set: retry_safe, state_isolated, result_safe, optional_safe, input_validated, pii_contained, injection_safe, canonical, cost_bounded. Note "fault_covered": false — good thing I didn't declare it. "pure" and "read_only" false — good.

So the Proof<...> properties must come from a fixed vocabulary — and maybe declaring a property outside that vocabulary (result_safe, optional_safe, canonical, cost_bounded, input_validated, pii_contained) is an error? But review_patch showed 0 violations... though review_patch may only check a subset (grammar/type violations?), whereas the full veto includes proof checks. Good, that's the known-good contract list. And review_patch reports no violations. Also note idempotent and deterministic are true here (better than the example), but I don't need to claim them — claiming them may be allowed but I'll keep the example's contract to be safe.

Now, one thing: since review_patch returned ok with 0 violations, I can propose. Should I add deterministic/idempotent claims? The user asked for a durable two-step workflow; the proof card will show idempotent true. Not necessary to declare. Keep minimal-risk contract.

Actually, hold on — should the declared Proof set include "idempotent"? Not required.

Let me now also double check the response body requirement: "Respond 201 with a body carrying reserved and charged as true." My body: `{ reserved: true, charged: true }` with status 201. Good.

The body also includes error body for missing key with 400 — that's a reasonable fallback and the durable example did the same. Fine.

Now propose_change_set with the exact content that passed review_patch (identical bytes to avoid surprises).

Careful: review_patch content I passed — I must reproduce exactly, including the multiline Proof union formatting. Let me reproduce verbatim.

One question: will the host veto possibly complain about the `if (key === undefined)` guard whose Response is a plain Response (not branded)? review_patch said no violations, which presumably includes type checking (it reported properties, so it ran the type checker). Good.

Propose now.","tool_calls":[{"index":0,"id":"call_00_VqZL1H4mcc40vl7XZWcD9048","type":"function","function":{"name":"propose_change_set","arguments":"{"changes": [{"file": "handler.ts", "content": "import { hmacSha256 } from \"zttp:crypto\";\nimport { run, step } from \"zttp:durable\";\n\nstructural OrderRun<T> = Proof<T,\n  | \"retry_safe\"\n  | \"state_isolated\"\n  | \"result_safe\"\n  | \"optional_safe\"\n  | \"input_validated\"\n  | \"pii_contained\"\n  | \"injection_safe\"\n  | \"canonical\"\n  | \"cost_bounded\"\n>;\n\nexport function handler(req: Request): OrderRun<Response> {\n  const key = req.headers.get(\"idempotency-key\");\n  if (key === undefined) {\n    return Response.json({ error: \"missing Idempotency-Key\" }, { status: 400 });\n  }\n  return run(key, () => {\n    step(\"reserve\", () => ({ reservationId: hmacSha256(key, \"reserve\") }));\n    step(\"charge\", () => ({ chargeId: hmacSha256(key, \"charge\") }));\n    return Response.json({ reserved: true, charged: true }, { status: 201 });\n  });\n}\n"}]}"}}]},"logprobs":null,"finish_reason":"tool_calls"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":11992,"completion_tokens":1130,"total_tokens":13122,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":3968},"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":779},"prompt_cache_hit_tokens":3968,"prompt_cache_miss_tokens":8024},"system_fingerprint":"aeb56401ca74e127821c4f9126dcb669"}
